newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Britain welcomes Swiss probe into Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Britain welcomes Swiss probe into Nazi gold.

text.p: Britain welcomed Swiss government efforts to clear up the fate of Nazi gold that may linger in Swiss bank vaults, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Wednesday.

Rifkind also told reporters relations between London and Berne were good, despite allegations raised by a British government report that the Swiss returned only about one-tenth of Nazi gold demanded by the Allies after World War Two.
"I very much welcome the announcement that was made by Swiss federal authorities earlier this week on setting up the comprehensive study into this question," Rifkind told a news conference.
"We have a superbly healthy relation," Rifkind said.

Rifkind spoke after meeting his Swiss counterpart, Flavio Cotti, for talks that included Berne's plans for a commission of experts to study the extent and fate of both Nazi and Jewish riches deposited in neutral Switzerland during World War Two.
Cotti told the joint news conference he was confident that the Swiss parliament would give final backing to legislation creating the historical commission after the cabinet backed the bill on Monday.
Rifkind called the commission on wartime wealth and Swiss banking an "appropriate and sensitive response. I very much welcome that response."

Swiss politicians have been drafting the commission bill since May in response to claims by world Jewish groups that secretive Swiss banks had not done enough to find and hand over accounts left by Jews killed in the Holocaust.

Berne came under added pressure for a comprehensive study of wartime financial deals from last week's British Foreign Office report on Nazi gold, which suggested the Swiss National Bank could be hoarding gold stolen by Hitler's Germany.
